title: Amendments to 100 Victoria Street encampment by-law
subtitle: Safe tenting protocol motion tied; SWIFT board reappointment; transition plan, later possession date, and no penalty for occupants.
overview: Regional Council held a special meeting to amend the by-law governing the use of 100 Victoria Street North in Kitchener, the site planned for the Kitchener Central Transit Hub. Council passed the amendment {{vote:m3}}. It moves the date for vacant possession to April 1, 2026, removes the offence penalty, and writes a transition plan into the by-law. The plan includes a mandatory written offer of alternative housing to people who occupied the site as of April 16, 2025.

Council also voted on a motion from one councillor to direct staff to report back on a safe tenting protocol by March 2026. It was defeated on a tie {{vote:m2}}. Staff said work on a broader encampment response protocol is already a 2026 priority under the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. Council reappointed Councillor Sue Foxton to the Southwestern Integrated Fibre Technology (SWIFT) board {{vote:m4}}.

For residents, the changes mean people at the site will not face fines. Staff said everyone living unsheltered will continue to be offered shelter or housing support. The by-law amendment will be filed in the ongoing court proceedings, and the court's order may lead to further changes.

decisions.item: 100 Victoria Street Code of Use amendment
decisions.detail: Council passed a by-law amending By-law 25-021 to defer possession to April 1, 2026, remove the offence penalty and codify a transition plan with written housing offers {{vote:m3}}.
Council enacted the by-law amending By-law 25-021 to facilitate the Kitchener Central Transit Hub and other transit development.
Council waived the notice requirement so a safe tenting motion could be considered at this meeting {{vote:m1}}.
A motion to direct staff to report back on a safe tenting protocol by March 2026 was defeated on a tie {{vote:m2}}.
Council reappointed Councillor Sue Foxton to the SWIFT Board of Directors {{vote:m4}}.

debate: Supporters of the safe tenting motion said staff should research protocols used in places such as Guelph, Hamilton, London and Peel, including what has and has not worked. They said a report would not commit council to adopting a protocol, and that delegates and the courts had pointed to the lack of a place of last resort.

Opponents said staff already have a heavy workload, and that the work should go into housing and the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. Some said a tenting protocol would accept people living outdoors, would duplicate unsafe conditions, or would shift the issue to area municipalities. Several noted that earlier last-resort sites such as Herb Street filled quickly.

Some councillors said area municipalities would need to be involved because a regional by-law would apply only to regional land. Staff said Peel's protocol was developed with its cities and with cost sharing. Staff also said a protocol would come from them, while any by-law would come from legal staff.

On the by-law amendment, one councillor opposed it, saying it would have little effect in court and that the Region needed a place of last resort. Others supported it as an improvement because it drops the monetary penalty and adds guaranteed offers. One said it was a step in the right direction.

Some councillors questioned how notice was given at the site, which was a notice posted in a plastic sleeve. Staff said it met legal requirements, and one councillor suggested photographing posted notices in future. Staff said the court's order will determine whether further changes are possible.
